sections.h2: Three ways to sell a Hempstead house
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or sell straight to a buyer who accepts the house with its flaws. The house's condition and your deadline should decide it.

About four in five Hempstead homes are owner-occupied, so your house competes with many similar ones on nearby blocks. If the roof, boiler and kitchen are sound, a listing aimed at a mortgage buyer tends to win the highest price. A house that needs heavy work, carries an estate problem or has a tenant who won't leave may lose that advantage to repair bills and waiting.

  • Agent listing: a commission, weeks of showings and a buyer whose lender must approve the loan, in return for the biggest pool of bidders.
  • Owner-run sale: your attorney drafts the contract while you handle photos, pricing and open houses.
  • Direct as-is purchase: little preparation, few contingencies and a date you help set, offset by a discounted price.

Ask each bidder to put the number, the date and the proof of money on paper, then subtract every cost to see what actually reaches you.

sections.h2: Which communities are in the Town of Hempstead
sections.html:
Hempstead takes up the southwest of Nassau County on Long Island, and no other town in New York State has more people. Its western boundary meets Queens. It contains 22 incorporated villages and 38 hamlets. Villages include Freeport, Garden City, Rockville Centre, Valley Stream, Lynbrook and the Village of Hempstead itself, while hamlets include Levittown, Baldwin, Oceanside, Uniondale, East Meadow and Wantagh. The village or hamlet is the first thing a buyer asks about, and the mailing address may say only Hempstead or a neighboring name, so spell it out.

Commuting runs on rail and parkways. The Long Island Rail Road crosses the town on a Main Line and Hempstead, West Hempstead, Babylon, Far Rockaway and Long Beach branches, and Nassau Inter-County Express buses fill in between stations. The Southern State, Meadowbrook and Wantagh parkways carry car traffic. If the house is a short walk from a station, lead with that in the listing.

Nearly 796,000 people live in the town, in about 250,600 households of roughly three people each. The estimate for 2025 is 795,734 residents and 250,622 households. Owners live in 82.2% of homes. The median owner-occupied home is worth $640,800, median monthly owner cost with a mortgage is $3,657, median rent is $2,101, median household income is $141,243, and the average trip to work takes 36.6 minutes.

With owner costs that high, taxes weigh heavily on buyers. If your own bill runs lower than similar listings nearby, say so early.

The Town of Hempstead Receiver of Taxes collects general and school taxes in four steps through the year. The same office collects for Nassau County, the town, 99 special districts and 33 school districts.

A buyer's attorney will want a printout of what is paid and what is still open on your parcel.

sections.h2: Challenging your assessment before you sell
sections.html:
Yes, it can be done before a sale. Nassau County runs assessment appeals through its Assessment Review Commission, and the next window runs from January 4, 2027 to March 1, 2027. Filing costs nothing and you don't need an attorney.

The commission can lower an assessment but never raise it. It also corrects a wrong tax class and reviews cases where an exemption was denied. Set the county's adjusted market value for your house beside your own sense of its sale price, and appeal if yours is clearly lower. If you file, tell the buyer an appeal is pending.

One warning: sign no more than one authorization for a grievance service, and don't file for yourself if you already authorized a representative, because duplicate applications left unresolved are denied. The office is at 240 Old Country Road, 5th Floor, Mineola, NY 11501, phone 516-571-3214, open weekdays until 4:30 in the afternoon. The window opens after the new year, so a listing that closes this fall can't use it.

sections.h2: Permits and the Department of Buildings
sections.html:
The Town of Hempstead Department of Buildings enforces the building, plumbing, electrical and housing codes, along with the rules for how land and buildings are used and occupied. It is at One Washington Street, 2nd Floor, Hempstead, NY 11550, phone 516-538-8500, with a front counter open from 8 am to 4:45 pm. Permits and forms go through the town's Online Permit Center. Housing and Zoning Inspectors take calls at 516-812-3289 from 9 am to 10:30 am, before they leave for field inspections.

Before you list, ask the department what permits are on file for any addition, finished basement, deck or second kitchen. A buyer's attorney will find work that was never permitted, and clearing it up before a contract is signed is quicker than doing it under a closing deadline.

Expect to owe $2 for each $500 of the price, with any leftover part of $500 counted as a full unit, unless your contract shifts that cost to the buyer. The tax is reported on Form TP-584 and filed where the deed is recorded. Sales of residential property at $1 million or more also trigger a separate 1% charge, and the buyer pays it.

The Nassau County Clerk records Hempstead deeds and maintains the official index of who owns real property in the county, with land documents searchable online. In most sales your attorney or the title company files everything for you.

sections.h2: Checking a cash offer on a Hempstead house
sections.html:
Judge an offer by what lands in your account, not by the headline price. A smaller offer with no repairs, no showings and a short fuse can leave you even with a bigger listing that carries commission and fix-up costs.

  • Insist on a written offer that names the closing date and shows proof of funds.
  • Settle who bears the transfer tax and the other closing costs before you sign.
  • Let your attorney read the contract, and confirm the deed goes to the Nassau County Clerk.
  • Call the Receiver of Taxes about any open installment so it is cleared at closing.
  • Line up two or three bids, plus an agent's estimate of a listing price.

faqs.q: Which office takes property tax payments in Hempstead?
faqs.a: The Town of Hempstead Receiver of Taxes does, from an office on North Franklin Street. It takes county, town, special district and school district payments, and 516-538-1500 reaches it.

faqs.q: Is the Village of Hempstead the same as the Town of Hempstead?
faqs.a: No. The village is one of 22 incorporated villages inside the much larger town, which also holds 38 hamlets such as Levittown and Uniondale. Name the exact village or hamlet when you describe your house to a buyer.

faqs.q: When can I file an assessment appeal in Nassau County?
faqs.a: The next window runs from January 4, 2027 through March 1, 2027. The county's Assessment Review Commission takes the filing free of charge and can only reduce an assessment.

faqs.q: Who pays the New York transfer tax when a house sells?
faqs.a: The seller, unless the contract says otherwise. The buyer is responsible for the extra 1% that applies once a residential price reaches $1 million.

faqs.q: Which office handles building permits in Hempstead?
faqs.a: The town's Department of Buildings, at One Washington Street in Hempstead, phone 516-538-8500. Applications go through its Online Permit Center.
